title: KS-160 Step 3: set tenant GUC on checkout + admin-role exemption for cross-tenant reads + flip fail-closed (atomic, dev-first)
description:
Steps 2-4 of the RLS fail-closed plan (PR #164 doc) — must land together (partial application breaks reads).

1. Tenant-pool-manager (or a query wrapper) sets `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction from the authenticated tenant context — for every tenant-scoped call site identified in [KS-172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-172/ks-160-step-1-inventory-tenant-scoped-vs-cross-tenant-query-paths-rls).
2. Route the cross-tenant-by-design reads (login `findByEmail`, register uniqueness, super-admin, provisioning) onto the RLS-exempt admin connection (`secuuraadmin` / `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`), per the decided admin-role-exemption approach.
3. Drop the `IS NULL`/`= ''` branches from the `tenant_isolation` policy → fail-closed.
4. Regression test: `secuura_app` + no GUC + `SELECT count(*) FROM users` → 0 rows.

**Blocked by** [KS-172](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-172/ks-160-step-1-inventory-tenant-scoped-vs-cross-tenant-query-paths-rls) (inventory). **Dev-first**, exercise login + every portal + e2e before any promotion; never onto the frozen demo until after the planned push.

nodes.title: feat(KS-174): tenant RLS fail-closed flip + regression test [DRAFT — do not merge]

nodes.body:
Superseded: KS-174 is closed as superseded by KS-458 (archived 2026-08-16, so Linear refuses a Duplicate relation to it); KS-458 holds the merged PRs 534 and 675.

* KS-458's own title names this ticket: "RLS fail-closed flip + GUC-on-checkout — flip the consolidated tenant_isolation policy fail-open → fail-closed (the never-filed "KS-174")". KS-458 is Done (completed 2026-08-12) and archived, and its scope and acceptance cover this ticket's four steps: the tenant GUC on checkout, the cross-tenant pre-auth lookups, the fail-closed policy, and a no-GUC zero-rows check.
* Delivered by PR 534 (squash 46fb9f88dfb1, merged 2026-07-14: migration 039, the GUC wiring in the services, fail-closed on 26 tables) and PR 675 (squash cda661416a77, merged 2026-08-12: the verify script's fail-closed set derived from the live policy).
* Design difference from this ticket's step 2: Kam's 2026-07-14 pick on KS-458 was option (a), SECURITY DEFINER lookups for the pre-auth login path, not the RLS-exempt admin connection this ticket names.
* PR 191, this ticket's only attachment, is closed and was never merged.
* KS-160 (the parent epic), read whole for this close: Done 2026-06-02; its only child is KS-172 (Done); its three comments (the premise finding, the Path A decision, the admin-authority refinement) name this ticket as step 3 and leave no residue against it. The 2026-09-08 comment on this ticket asked that it be checked against KS-160's closure: checked, consistent.
* Running-build ancestry, not a live check: the squash of PR 534 is an ancestor of every recorded Kintsugi per-service base (6c9a593df4ab, 35bcfa000b44, c5c26b2835df, ee1e1b832115) and the squash of PR 675 is an ancestor of 6c9a593df4ab and c5c26b2835df, by GitHub compare with a reverse control, read 2026-11-11. Migration 039 on kintsugi: UNREAD.
* No follow-up key: KS-458 is the record.

## Unarchived on Kam's ruling

Kam ruled `three` on the card `secuura-61-archived-while-still-open`: **unarchive only the three `In Progress` tickets** of the 61 archived-while-still-open, and nothing else. Relayed in Wednesday's GO mail of 2026-09-08T04:02:45Z, **DKIM-verified as her relay** (3 pass values, all 8 failing-value controls absent) — relayed from his card, not independently verified as his own words.

**Restored cleanly, and measured:** archived-non-terminal KS issues **72 → 69**, the set that left the archive is exactly `{KS-174, KS-796, KS-802}`, and **nothing entered the archive unexpectedly**. That census delta is the instrument, not the parent-side child query — on an archived parent that query returns 0 children whether or not there are any, which is the blind spot [KS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-995) records.

**Parent is KS-160, which is `Done`.** This ticket is back in `In Progress` because that is the state it was archived from — not a claim that the work is outstanding. Whoever picks it up should check it against KS-160's closure before doing anything.

**Full portal e2e done — issuer verified working end-to-end under fail-closed** (pushed `096af3f6e`).

**Found + fixed a second wiring gap:** originate only registered `extractTenantContext` when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, but the platform runs single-tenant — so the ALS was never populated and `queryWithTenant` set no GUC, fail-closing every tenant read to 0. Added an **always-on ALS-binding middleware** in originate (`x-tenant-id || DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, matching `getReqTenantId`'s app-level filter so GUC and `WHERE tenant_id` always agree).

**Verified on the live `secuura_app` stack, fail-closed (032):**
- **issuer@secuura.com → `GET /api/documents` = 15** — identical to the permissive baseline (15). End-to-end through gateway → originate → pgbouncer.
- **Issuer portal renders under fail-closed** — dashboard loads, document list + on-chain status display (browser, demo user: 3 docs). Screenshot captured.
- Login + `/me` OK; all services healthy; local stack restored to develop/permissive after (issuer back to 15).

**Note on the seed data (surfaced by this test):** default-tenant *users* carry `tenant_id=00000…1` while their *documents* carry `a0000…1` (the canonical `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`). They must be the same tenant — under fail-closed a user only sees docs whose `tenant_id` matches their GUC, so this inconsistency would hide default-tenant docs. **Filing a seed-fix follow-up** (align default-tenant users to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`). Verified the e2e by aligning locally → issuer correctly saw the 15.

**Still remaining (smaller):**
1. Registry verify-by-hash tenant-unscoped fix (authenticated cross-tenant verify).
2. **super_admin / SYSTEM_ADMIN** document views: admin (no tenant) saw 25 in permissive via the now-removed X-Tenant-Override; under fail-closed → 0. This is the admin-dashboard product call (you chose "drop ambient cross-tenant views") — confirm admin keeps system/user-mgmt only, then this is correct-as-is.

#191 (draft) now has the migration + regression test + auth + originate wiring + the GUC mechanism proven through pgbouncer AND through the live portal. The critical user-facing path (login + document list) works under fail-closed.

**originate/gateway wiring done + GUC mechanism PROVEN end-to-end through pgbouncer** (pushed to #191, commits `37e7b3d89`, `5d148ea5b`).

**Added this pass:**
- originate's 247 raw `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` calls now route through `queryWithTenant` (via `createPoolProxy`), in BOTH multi-tenant and single-tenant (Prisma-fallback) modes — so document/tenant-table reads set `app.current_tenant_id`. `withTenant` (KS-108, `app.tenant_id` for rights_holders) is untouched (proxy detects pool vs txn-client).
- `createPgPool()` added to `@secuura/shared` (originate has no direct `pg` dep — the dynamic require failed at runtime).
- **Fixed a real pgbouncer bug in `queryWithTenant`:** the original set the GUC session-scoped on a checked-out client, but under pgbouncer transaction-pooling consecutive autocommit statements can hit different server connections, so the SELECT might not see the GUC. Now wrapped in ONE transaction with `set_config(is_local=true)` — pins them together, auto-discards at COMMIT (no RESET/leak).

**VERIFIED (live `secuura_app` stack, fail-closed 032, through pgbouncer):**
- `secuura_app` no GUC → documents **0** (fail-closed); `BEGIN; set_config('app.current_tenant_id', <tenant>, true); SELECT → 25` (the tenant's docs); after COMMIT → **0** (no leak). The exact queryWithTenant pattern, proven pgbouncer-safe.
- auth login + `/api/auth/me` OK (OWNER no-tenant via exempt; tenant user).
- originate + api-gateway boot healthy under fail-closed.
- All four packages compile in the real Docker build.
- Local stack restored to develop/permissive after.

**Remaining before enabling on an env:**
1. **`platform_document_registry` verify-by-hash** (`originate/routes/verification.ts`) is cross-tenant by design — an *authenticated* caller now has a GUC bound, so that specific read must run tenant-unscoped (`runWithTenant(undefined, …)` or a dedicated non-GUC query). Public/unauthenticated verify is fine (no GUC). Targeted fix.
2. api-gateway service-level `query()` (admin user-management = bucket B / control-plane) — review whether it needs exempt vs GUC.
3. Full portal + e2e on a `secuura_app` stack (the seed data has the issuer in tenant `00000…1` while docs are in `a0000…1`, so portal-doc checks need a user whose tenant owns docs).

#191 stays a draft (do-not-merge) for Peter/Stuart review; the core mechanism + critical paths are now proven, not theoretical.

**Wiring built + the critical path VERIFIED end-to-end under fail-closed** (pushed to #191; commits up to `2134c9a61`).

**Implemented (all compile in the real Docker build — auth + api-gateway built clean):**
- Per-request GUC mechanism: `shared/db/tenant-als.ts` (AsyncLocalStorage + `queryWithTenant` — sets `app.current_tenant_id` session-scope on a checked-out client, RESET before release; no tenant bound → plain query). Bound by `authenticate()` (JWT tenantId) + `extractTenantContext` (x-tenant-id).
- auth identity lookups (`getUserByEmail`/`getUserBySocialId`/`emailExists`/`getUserById`) → RLS-exempt admin connection (`MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`, falls back to DATABASE_URL). `getUserById` matters because platform users have no tenant_id → GUC can't be set; fetching your own record by id is identity, not enumeration.
- auth `query()` shared-pool path → `queryWithTenant`.
- api-gateway: X-Tenant-Override ambient path **removed** (tenant always from JWT; override header stripped).
- `startup-migrations.ts`: the 4 inline policies flipped to strict in lockstep with 032.

**VERIFIED on a live `secuura_app` stack (Docker up), fail-closed 032 applied + auth given an exempt `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`:**
- `secuura_app` + no GUC on `users` → **0 rows** (fail-closed live).
- Login OWNER (demo@secuura.io, no tenant) → 200 + token; `GET /api/auth/me` → 200.
- Login tenant user (issuer@secuura.com) → 200 + token; `/me` → 200.
- Regression test passes; GUC set_config → correct per-tenant rows (SQL-proven).
- Local stack restored to develop/permissive afterward.

**Remaining before the flip can be ENABLED on an env (itemised honestly):**
1. **Wire originate + api-gateway service `query()` to `queryWithTenant`** (same pattern as auth) — else tenant DATA reads (documents, etc.) return 0 under fail-closed and the issuer/verifier portals show empty. This is the next chunk.
2. Set `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` for auth in **local** compose (prod already has it via bicep) if we want local to run fail-closed.
3. Full portal + e2e on the `secuura_app` stack.

So: the highest-risk path (auth/login — an outage if it broke) is proven safe under fail-closed. #190 (KS-173) + #191 (KS-174) stay as review PRs (not merged). Recommend the originate/gateway `query()` delegation + portal e2e as the close-out.

**Wiring progress (pushed to #191):**
- ✅ **Login-exempt-conn done** (`ed6f574c9`) — `getAdminPool()`/`adminQuery()` in `auth/db.ts` (MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL, falls back to DATABASE_URL); `getUserByEmail`/`getUserBySocialId`/`emailExists` now run on the RLS-exempt connection. Typechecks (`tsc --noEmit`, auth).

**What going deeper revealed about the remaining work — it's the broad cross-cutting piece, not a bounded edit:**
- It isn't just *login*. **Every authed request** calls `getUserById` against the shared `secuura` DB (`users`), which the inventory classifies bucket-A (tenant-scoped). Under fail-closed + `secuura_app` + no GUC → 0 rows → the request fails. Same for any other shared-DB tenant-table read.
- So a *working* flip needs the **tenant GUC set per-request on the shared-DB pool** from the JWT's tenant context — across auth (post-login user reads), api-gateway, originate. The clean way is a request-scoped mechanism (AsyncLocalStorage holding tenantId, set by the tenant-context middleware) + a shared-pool query wrapper that sets `app.current_tenant_id` (transaction-local) for the query — so call sites don't each change. `withTenantContext` is the seed of this but has 0 callers.
- This is exactly what RLS-FAIL-CLOSED-PLAN.md calls *"the cross-cutting step (touches every tenant-scoped service)"* and must be verified on a `secuura_app` full stack (login + every portal + e2e), dev-first.

**Recommendation:** the GUC-request-context mechanism + full-stack `secuura_app` verification is a focused effort of its own (genuinely the bulk of KS-174's risk). The migration + regression test (proven) + login-exempt-conn are banked on #191. X-Tenant-Override drop + the 4 startup-migrations strict bodies are quick and should land *with* the GUC mechanism (so nothing's half-flipped). Flagging to Kam before building the request-context plumbing.

Started — draft PR **#191** (stacked on #190 / KS-173). **Security core proven; app-wiring remaining.**

**Done + verified (Docker up this session):**
- `migrations/032_rls_fail_closed.sql` — strict policy (drops `IS NULL`/`''`), `platform_document_registry` excluded (verify-by-hash).
- `migrations/__tests__/rls_fail_closed.test.sql` — self-contained regression test (provisions a NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role), passes.
- **Proven on the real `secuura` DB (20 users / 7 tenants):** secuura_app no-GUC → permissive 20 vs **strict 0**; GUC=tenant → 5 (isolated); owner/exempt → 20. So the flip works, isolation binds, and login (`getUserByEmail`, no tenant context) **provably returns 0 under fail-closed** → confirms the exempt-connection requirement. Local DB restored to permissive after.

**Remaining (the "keep the app working under fail-closed" half — needs a `secuura_app` full-stack to verify):**
1. GUC-on-checkout in `tenant-pool-manager.ts` (`tenantTransaction` L341 / `tenantQuery` L326).
2. Login `getUserByEmail` + register uniqueness via the RLS-exempt admin connection (`userRepo.ts:262`).
3. Drop the X-Tenant-Override ambient cross-tenant path (`api-gateway/middleware/auth.ts:281`).
4. Flip the 4 `startup-migrations.ts` inline policies to strict in lockstep.
5. Verify login + portals + e2e on a `secuura_app` stack (`APP_DB_PASSWORD` set), dev-first.

This is a substantial cross-service change best done as a focused pass with the secuura_app stack up — flagged to Kam for go-ahead before grinding the wiring.

## Scoping pass (2026-06-03) — attempted the flip, surfaced two hard blockers + a bigger surface than the inventory showed

Kam's calls for this work (2026-06-03): **bucket C = fail-closed is correct** — drop ambient cross-tenant data views, remove the X-Tenant-Override ambient data path (admin keeps system/user-management only); **land as a CI-green PR for Peter/Stuart review, do NOT merge** until verified.

While scoping the implementation I hit two things that make a safe, *verified* flip impossible in a general session and bigger than KS-172's first pass:

### Blocker 1 — the policy lives in **12 places**, not one
The fail-open `tenant_isolation` policy (`current_setting('app.current_tenant_id',true) IS NULL OR ='' OR tenant_id::text = …`) is created in: migrations **009, 011, 012, 013, 014, 015, 017, 018, 022, 023, 024** and **`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`**. Tables span `users, oauth_apps, tenant_config, tenant_contacts, vault_entries, svc_webhooks, platform_document_registry` (009) + `documents, custody_events, shares` (startup-migrations) + `organizations, svc_api_keys, svc_dids, admin_verification_queue, issuer_certs, rights_holders, charge/peer tables` (011–024). A partial flip leaves a mixed fail-open/fail-closed schema. **→ KS-173 (consolidate 12 → 1 authoritative migration, still fail-open) is a true prerequisite and is itself non-trivial; do it first.**

### Blocker 2 — not verifiable without a `secuura_app` stack
RLS only binds for a non-superuser/non-BYPASSRLS role. `provisionAppRole` (startup-migrations.ts) is **gated on `APP_DB_PASSWORD`**; unset locally → the stack runs as a superuser → **the flip is inert and untestable**. Same in GitHub CI (no APP_DB_PASSWORD → superuser → CI would stay green while the policy does nothing AND while login silently breaks under a real least-priv role). So neither local-default nor CI can verify this. Verification requires either (a) a local stack reconfigured with `APP_DB_PASSWORD` so `secuura_app` is provisioned, or (b) Azure dev (already runs as `secuura_app`, KS-109). Docker was also down this session, so even the throwaway-postgres proof of the policy SQL wasn't runnable.

### Implementation-ready plan (for the dedicated session, Docker up)
1. **KS-173 first** — consolidate all 12 policy definitions into one migration, behaviour-neutral (still fail-open). One source of truth.
2. **Exclude `platform_document_registry`** from the strict policy (bucket D — public verify-by-hash is cross-tenant by design; keep a permissive policy or a dedicated read connection).
3. **GUC-on-checkout** — shared `secuura` DB pool: `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction (`tenant-pool-manager.ts` `tenantTransaction` L341; `tenantQuery` L326 has no transaction → must wrap or adopt `withTenantContext`). Per-tenant pools: set via the pool `connect` handler (each pool already knows its tenant).
4. **Bucket B via admin/exempt connection** — auth `findByEmail` (login) + register uniqueness; api-gateway `admin.ts` user-management; tenant-provisioning. (Login is the linchpin — breaks first if missed.)
5. **Bucket C removed** (per Kam) — drop adminConfig cross-tenant document/business aggregates + the X-Tenant-Override ambient data path.
6. **Flip fail-closed** — drop the `IS NULL`/`=''` branches in the consolidated migration.
7. **Regression test** — connect as `secuura_app` (no GUC) → `SELECT count(*) FROM users` = 0; with GUC → rows. The acceptance proof.
8. Verify: login + each portal + e2e on the `secuura_app` stack, dev-first.

Recommend running this as its own focused session with Docker up. Docs (plan #164, inventory #165) are merged; KS-172 closed. KS-160/KS-173/KS-174 left open with this plan.
